The mist is slow this morning. I do not mind. Sit if you like.
A cold tide keeps the fish honest. You are up early. So am I.
The heron watches us from the reeds. He always watches. Patience, friend.
My boat creaks like an old man. Heh. Same as me, mostly.
Slow water hides quick fish. That is the whole trick of it.
You walk soft for a stranger. The pond likes that. So do I.
Bait waits for no one. Well, it waits. That is all it does.
The wind turned east last night. Fish feel it first. So does my knee.
A knot tied in haste undoes itself in the dark. Mind your hands, friend.
Morning fog means a long day. The kettle is still warm. Sit.
The tide is neither kind nor cruel. It is only patient. Like us.
My net has three holes. The fish know. Word travels fast.
You have a fisherman's quiet. That is rare. Welcome to Nekomura.
The pond is older than the village. It keeps our secrets. And my boots.
A heron stole my catch at dawn. Heh. Bold bird. Worse neighbors, truly.
Sit on the crate. The dock is damp. Everything here is damp.
Fish do not hurry. Nor do I. We both get there eventually.
The morning mist burned off by noon. My line stayed lazy. So did I.
You greet me like an old friend. I am not one yet. Give it a season.
A bent hook teaches more than ten straight ones. Take my spare.
The tide came in and took my hat. Heh. Rude, the sea.
Sometimes the fish simply win. That is fair. They live here too.
My oars are chipped from years of use. Like me. Still good enough.
Cold mornings make hot soup worth it. That is my whole philosophy.
The heron and I have an agreement. He steals. I grumble. We continue.
The bait box is nearly empty. So is the morning. Both fill again.
Wind from the north means rain by dusk. Fish bite before storms. So do I.
I talk to the pond sometimes. It listens better than most folks.
You stand like someone waiting for the tide. It comes. It always comes.
The old cat naps on my tackle box. He has the right idea. Heh.
A line in still water still catches hope. That is enough for today.
My boots squelch when I walk. The fish hear me coming. Oh well.
The village wakes slow. That suits a fisherman. And his knees.
Cast where the reeds bend. Fish hide in the shade. Simple as that.
You have kind eyes for a stranger. The village will notice. It notices everything.
The tide table is a suggestion. The fish write their own. So do the gulls.
Rain on the pond makes rings like coins. I never learned to spend them.
An old net mends slow but mends true. Same with most things.
The sun is up and the fish are not. We wait together, you and I.
My boat is named Patience. That is a joke. Heh. Mostly a joke.
You do not rush your greeting. I appreciate that in a person.
The heron flew off when you came. He trusts you already. Fickle bird.
A fisherman counts his catches and his blessings. Fewer of one, more of the other.
The dock boards are warm now. Sit before the tide turns cold.
Fish remember the hook, not the hand. Curious, is it not?
Morning is the honest hour. The pond tells the truth then. So do I.
I have mended this net since spring. It is mostly knots now. Heh.
The mist hangs low on the far bank. Something is hiding. Probably nothing.
You came down the path quietly. Most visitors clomp. Good sign.
A slow cast reaches farther than a fast one. Live and learn.
My kettle sings at dawn. The fish do not care. I do.
The tide will turn in an hour. Or not. It keeps its own counsel.
An old cat knows which dock boards creak. So do I. Useful knowledge.
The village is small but the pond is deep. Both have room for you.
Wind ripples the water and the fish stop thinking. So do I, sometimes.
A cheap hook bends. A good one waits. Choose your tackle wisely.
You look like you have questions. The pond has answers. Slow ones.
The heron left a feather on my boat. A gift or a taunt. Heh. The nerve.
Fish rise at dawn and at dusk. The rest is just standing around.
My back aches before rain. Better than any barometer. Useless for fishing.
